knowledge:
- key_parameters: inputFileName=The path to a tab-separated text file containing the network configuration with columns 'type' and 'file_name' ;; numCores=Number of CPU cores to use for parallel processing (defaults to 1; highly recommended to use all available cores when generating p-values) ;; delta=Probability of jumping between gene layers (default is 0.5) ;; zeta=Probability of jumping between phenotype layers (default is 0.5) ;; lambda=Inter-network jump probability between gene and phenotype networks (default is 0.5) ;; geneSeeds=Vector of gene IDs where the RWR starts ;; phenoSeeds=Vector of phenotype IDs where the RWR starts ;; generatePValue=Logical determining whether to calculate empirical p-values along with ranks (defaults to TRUE in some signatures) ;; S=Number of random runs for empirical p-value calculation (default is 1000) ;; r=Restart probability of RWR (default is 0.7) ;; eta=Controls restarting of RWR to either a gene seed or phenotype seed (default is 0.5; higher values utilize the phenotype network more) ;; tau=Vector of weights for each gene layer (must sum up to the total number of gene layers) ;; phi=Vector of weights for each phenotype layer (must sum up to the total number of phenotype layers)
- alternatives: None mentioned in the documentation.
- when_to_use: Use when you have multiplex (multi-layer) gene networks, multiplex phenotype networks, and bipartite gene-phenotype association networks, and you want to prioritize genes or phenotypes starting from a set of seed nodes.
- pitfalls: If generatePValue is set to TRUE, the execution time can be long, so using multiple cores via numCores is strongly recommended. The sum of the weights in the tau parameter must equal the number of gene layers, and the sum of the weights in the phi parameter must equal the number of phenotype layers. In the bipartite network file, the 'from' column must strictly contain gene IDs and the 'to' column must strictly contain phenotype IDs.

workflows.name: multiplex_heterogeneous_rwr_prioritization
workflows.intent: Prioritize genes and phenotypes using Random Walk with Restart on a multiplex heterogeneous network, with optional empirical p-value calculation.
input: input_file.txt (tab-separated text file listing network layer types and filenames)
gene_layer1.txt (tab-separated network file with columns 'from', 'to', and 'weight')
ptype_layer1.txt (tab-separated network file with columns 'from', 'to', and 'weight')
gene_ptype.txt (tab-separated bipartite network file with columns 'from' for genes, 'to' for phenotypes, and 'weight')
workflows.stages: 1. Load and inspect the network configuration and layer files ;; 2. Generate the transition walk matrix using CreateWalkMatrix ;; 3. Run the Random Walk with Restart algorithm using RandomWalkRestart with specified seeds and parameters to obtain ranked nodes and scores.
workflows.code:
inputDf <- read.table(system.file("extdata", "input_file.txt", package = "PhenoGeneRanker"), header=TRUE, sep="\t", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
print(inputDf)
geneLayerDf <- read.table(system.file("extdata", inputDf$file_name[1], package = "PhenoGeneRanker"), header=TRUE, sep="\t", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
print(head(geneLayerDf))
ptypeLayerDf <- read.table(system.file("extdata", inputDf$file_name[3], package = "PhenoGeneRanker"), header=TRUE, sep="\t", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
print(head(ptypeLayerDf))
biLayerDf <- read.table(system.file("extdata", inputDf$file_name[5], package = "PhenoGeneRanker"), header=TRUE, sep="\t", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
print(head(biLayerDf))
walkMatrix <- CreateWalkMatrix('input_file.txt')
ranks <- RandomWalkRestart(walkMatrix, c('g1', 'g5'), c("p1"), S=50) 
print(head(ranks))
ranks <- RandomWalkRestart(walkMatrix, c('g1'), c('p1', 'p2'), generatePValue=FALSE) 
print(head(ranks))
ranks <- RandomWalkRestart(walkMatrix, c('g1'), c(), TRUE, r=0.8, eta=0.6, tau=c(0.5,  1.5), phi=c(1.5, 0.5)) 
print(head(ranks))
